note: Generated from the Python reference implementation; do not edit by hand. Every case feeds its runs to a fresh MorseDecoder, applies the idle probes in order, then calls idle(+Infinity); 'text' is decoder.text afterwards.

params.run_format: [on, blocks]; a run lasts blocks * block_ms milliseconds
params.run_generation: pattern ms -> blocks = max(1, round(ms / block_ms)); marks +offset_ms, gaps -offset_ms

goertzel.power: 4 * |X(f0)|^2 / N^2 over the single bin at f0; a full-scale sine at f0 gives 1.0

decoder_constants.percentile_method: nearest rank: sort ascending, take the element at 1-based rank ceil(q / 100 * n)

cases.name: sos-15wpm-clean
cases.description: SOS keyed at 15 WPM with exact standard timing (80 ms dit, 240 ms dah).

cases.name: hello-world-8wpm
cases.description: HELLO WORLD at 8 WPM (150 ms dit): letter gaps and one word gap.

cases.name: jitter-20pct-12wpm-seed1
cases.description: HELLO WORLD at 12 WPM (100 ms dit), every run scaled by a uniform factor in 1 +- 0.2 drawn from numpy.random.default_rng(1).

parameters.rng: numpy.random.default_rng(seed): each run's ms is scaled by 1 + uniform(-jitter, jitter), one draw per run in order

cases.name: reverb-30ms-15wpm
cases.description: SOS at 15 WPM with a 30 ms reverb offset: marks measure 110/270 ms, gaps 50/210 ms (docs/PLAN.md section 4); the decoder must recover d = 30 ms.

cases.name: speed-change-12-to-6wpm
cases.description: PARIS PARIS at 12 WPM, a 7-dit word gap at the slower speed, then PARIS PARIS PARIS PARIS at 6 WPM. While the 100 ms dits drain out of the 30-run window the 200 ms dits sit exactly on the 2T boundary, so the transitional text depends on the nearest-rank percentile.
cases.text_before_idle: PARIS PARIS TTNARIS PARIS PARIS PARI
cases.text: PARIS PARIS TTNARIS PARIS PARIS PARIS

cases.name: oso-15wpm-dah-leading
cases.description: OSO at 15 WPM: the message opens with a dah-only letter. The first runs are held back until both mark classes have been seen, then replayed; the old seed-based rule read this as SSO.

cases.name: sos-hello-3wpm
cases.description: SOS HELLO at 3 WPM (400 ms dit): slow keying, held back until the first dah of O.

cases.name: hello-world-2wpm
cases.description: HELLO WORLD at 2 WPM (600 ms dit), the slowest supported speed.

cases.name: lone-o-idle-flush
cases.description: O alone at 15 WPM, then silence: three equal marks 3x the intra gaps. Three marks make the estimate trusted and the dah rule gives T = 80 ms, so idle() flushes once off_ms > 7T = 560 (560 is not > 560, 570 is).

cases.name: glitches-after-hello-8wpm
cases.description: HELLO WORLD at 8 WPM followed by keyboard clicks: 20 to 50 ms marks separated by 2 to 3 s of silence. Once the estimate is trusted, marks shorter than 0.4 T are ignored and leave the timing untouched.

cases.name: slowdown-20-to-4wpm
cases.description: PARIS at 20 WPM, a word gap at the slow speed, then HELLO WORLD at 4 WPM. Three marks of at least 1.5 T with no dit between them mean the estimate is stale-low: the window is rebuilt from those runs and the letter in progress re-read, so only the first slow letter is damaged.

cases.name: unknown-symbol
cases.description: Six dits in one letter (not in the table), a word gap, then S: emits '?' once and counts it in unknown_count.

cases.name: idle-flush
cases.description: SOS at 15 WPM with no gap after the last dit, so the last S is pending when the runs end. idle(off_ms) flushes it only once off_ms + offset_ms > 7 * dit_ms (560 is not > 560, 570 is) and later calls emit nothing.
